EXPLORER 2 · LESSON 6

First Actions & Body Parts for Babies 9–12 Months

Age 9–12 MonthsSubject Talk & ThinkClass Baby 2Duration 3–5 minutes

Between nine and twelve months, babies become little copiers: they wave, clap, point and love it when you name what they are doing. This class uses twelve simple cards — a hand, a foot, eyes, a nose, a mouth, then clapping, waving, eating, drinking, sleeping, pointing and smiling — shown one at a time while you say the word or do the action together.

There is no script and nothing to test. You talk and play, your baby looks and moves, and the words for their little body and everyday actions grow out of real, happy moments. Short sessions of three to five minutes are all it takes.

Start Today’s Class ↓Twelve cards, one at a time. Say the word, do the action — copy-me play wins at this age.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your baby has connected five body words to their own body, copied at least one action, and waved or pointed with meaning.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello, my little copier! Today we talk about YOU.”

    How: Have your baby on your lap — this class uses their own hands and feet as the props.

  2. Part 1 · Your body (cards 1–5)
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Hand

    “Hand! Where is your hand? Here is your hand!”

    How: Hold up your baby’s hand as you say it. Their own body makes the word impossible to miss.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Foot

    “Foot! Toot-toot, little foot.”

    How: Tap soles together gently as you sing it. Rhythm plus body word equals memory glue.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Eyes

    “Eyes! I see you with my eyes.”

    How: Point to the card’s eyes, then your eyes, then your baby’s. Three stops, one word.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Nose

    “Nose. Beep your little nose!”

    How: A gentle nose-beep makes the word a game. Games get requested — and requests mean repetition.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Mouth

    “Mouth! Open wide, mouth.”

    How: Open your own mouth wide as you say it. Copy-me play starts here.

  8. Part 2 · Your actions (cards 6–12)
  9. 07
    Card 6 · Clapping

    “Clap, clap! Clap your hands!”

    How: Bring your baby’s hands together gently on each clap. The action IS the word.

  10. 08
    Card 7 · Waving

    “Wave bye-bye!”

    How: Wave at the card, then wave at something real — a sibling, the window, someone leaving. Bye-bye becomes usable instantly.

  11. 09
    Card 8 · Eating

    “Eating! Yum-yum-yum.”

    How: Rub your tummy in circles, then say eating again at the next meal — same word, real moment.

  12. 10
    Card 9 · Drinking

    “Drinking — glug, glug!”

    How: Mime a sip. Name it again at the next bottle or cup for the second half of the lesson.

  13. 11
    Card 10 · Sleeping

    “Shhh… sleeping. Baby is sleeping.”

    How: Drop to a whisper with hands under your cheek. Whispering makes this the easiest word of the set.

  14. 12
    Card 11 · Pointing

    “Point! Point at… the teddy!”

    How: Point at a real object, then help your baby’s finger do it. Pointing is the wordless version of what is that?

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Smiling

    “A smile! Give me a big smile!”

    How: Smile big and wait — babies mirror faces. Their smile back is the check mark on the whole class.

  16. 14
    Practice

    “Your turn! Can you clap? Can you wave?”

    How: Ask for one action, wait five seconds, then help gently. Praise any attempt — a wiggle toward clapping counts.

  17. 15
    Check

    “Where are your eyes? Where is your foot?”

    How: Ask for one body part. A look, a touch or a wiggle toward it is correct. Nothing? Show it yourself and move on — this is not a test.

  18. 16
    Well done

    “Class finished! Hands, feet, claps and waves — clever body!”

    How: Use one class word in real life today (wave bye-bye to the bath). Real-life reuse turns today’s words into tomorrow’s talking.

Read the script while you show the cards above — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines quietly explain the trick behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.

PARENT INSTRUCTIONS

How to use this activity

Sit with your baby when they are awake, comfortable and interested. Show one card at a time and say the word or action naturally. Keep your language short and clear.

For example: ‘Hand.’ ‘These are eyes.’ ‘Clap, clap!’ ‘Wave bye-bye.’ ‘Baby is sleeping.’

When possible, connect the picture to your baby’s own body or to an action you can do together. For example, say ‘hand’ while gently showing your own hand, or clap your hands while saying ‘clap’.

Give your baby time to look, listen, move or respond in their own way. There is no need to test them or expect them to copy every action.

Keep the activity short and stop when your baby loses interest.

Every baby develops differently. Kiddo School age ranges are guides, not tests or developmental deadlines.

TRY TOGETHER

Little things to say.

Prompts for you, not for the cards — say them softly while your baby looks.

  • Where are your hands? Here are your hands.
  • Clap, clap!
  • Wave bye-bye.
  • Point!
  • Smile!
  • Time to sleep.
REAL-WORLD CONNECTION

Practice in Real Life

Continue the lesson naturally during your day.

  • During dressing: “Foot.”
  • During bath time: “Hand.”
  • When someone leaves: “Wave bye-bye.”
  • During play: “Clap, clap!”
  • When baby smiles: “Smile!”
